title: Adverbs of place, direction, frequency and time
summary: Тонкости наречий места и направления (**abroad, home, upstairs, everywhere**), частоты (**hardly ever, twice a week**) и времени (**still / yet / already, ago / before, lately, eventually**).
ru:
## Место и направление: без лишнего предлога
Многие наречия места уже содержат идею направления, поэтому предлог перед ними не нужен.
> She lives **abroad**, and we're going **abroad** next year. — Она живёт за границей, и мы едем за границу в следующем году.
> Let's go **home**. / Come **inside**. / Go **upstairs**. — Пойдём домой / войдите / поднимитесь наверх.
- ~~to abroad~~, ~~to home~~, ~~to downstairs~~, ~~to there~~ → **abroad, home, downstairs, there** (без to).
- Но существительное **home** с предлогом возможно: *She stayed at home. They returned to their home.*
Направление: **forward(s), backward(s), upward(s), downward(s)** — в американском варианте чаще без -s, в британском допустимы оба; *toward / towards* — тоже US / UK. **Northward, eastward** — формальные.
> The line moved **forward** slowly. — Очередь медленно двигалась вперёд.

## Неопределённость: somewhere, anywhere, everywhere, nowhere
- **somewhere** — в утверждении: *She's somewhere in Asia.*
- **anywhere** — в вопросе и отрицании: *I can't find it anywhere.*
- **everywhere / nowhere** — «повсюду / нигде»: *I've looked everywhere.* **nowhere** уже содержит отрицание: ~~I can't find it nowhere~~ → I can't find it **anywhere**.

## Частота: от «всегда» до «никогда»
Шкала: **always → usually → often → sometimes → occasionally → rarely / seldom → hardly ever → never**. Для точной частоты — выражения в конце: **twice a week, every other day, once in a while, from time to time**.
> I **hardly ever** work on Sundays. = I work on Sundays **very rarely**.
> We meet **twice a month**. — Мы встречаемся дважды в месяц.
> **ever** после отрицания усиливает его: *I don't ever want to see him.* (= I never want to see him.) — Я больше не хочу его видеть никогда.
- ~~hardly never~~ → **hardly ever** (двойное отрицание).

## Время: ago, before, since, for
- **ago** считает от **сейчас**: *She left three days ago.* (+ past simple)
- **before** — от момента в прошлом (past perfect): *She had left three days before.*
- **for** + период, **since** + точка отсчёта: *for ten years / since 2015.*
- **already** — раньше, чем ожидали; **still** — продолжается дольше ожидаемого; **yet** — в отрицании и вопросе, «до сих пор не»; **no longer / not ... any more** — перестало быть.
> Have you finished **yet**? — I've **already** done it. — Закончил? — Уже.
> She **still** hasn't replied, and he's **no longer** waiting. — Она всё ещё не ответила, а он больше не ждёт.

## Время: «недавно» и «наконец»
- **lately / recently**: *I haven't seen her **lately**.* (с perfect) / *He **recently** moved to Rome.* (с simple).
- **just** — «только что»: *The train has **just** left.*
- **finally / at last / eventually / in the end**: **finally** — после ожидания; **at last** — с облегчением; **eventually** — спустя долгое время, чаще после проблем; **in the end** — итог выбора или процесса.
> It took hours, but they **eventually** found the road. — Это заняло часы, но дорогу они в итоге нашли.
- **at the moment / currently** — «сейчас»; **presently** — BrE «скоро», AmE «сейчас».
- **later / afterwards / then / after that**: *Ten years **later** she opened a shop.* — Через десять лет она открыла магазин.

## Типичные ошибки
- ~~We went to abroad.~~ → We went **abroad**.
- ~~I have seen him yesterday.~~ → I **saw** him yesterday.
- ~~I know him since two years.~~ → I have known him **for** two years.
- ~~She is ill since Monday.~~ → She **has been** ill **since** Monday.
en:
## Place and direction: no extra preposition
Many adverbs of place already contain the idea of direction, so no preposition is used before them.
> She lives **abroad**, and we're going **abroad** next year.
> Let's go **home**. / Come **inside**. / Go **upstairs**.
- ~~to abroad~~, ~~to home~~, ~~to downstairs~~, ~~to there~~ → **abroad, home, downstairs, there** (no to).
- But the noun **home** can take a preposition: *She stayed at home. They returned to their home.*
Direction: **forward(s), backward(s), upward(s), downward(s)** — American English prefers the form without -s, British English allows both; *toward / towards* similarly. **Northward, eastward** are formal.
> The line moved **forward** slowly.

## Vague place: somewhere, anywhere, everywhere, nowhere
- **somewhere** — in positive statements: *She's somewhere in Asia.*
- **anywhere** — in questions and negatives: *I can't find it anywhere.*
- **everywhere / nowhere**: *I've looked everywhere.* **nowhere** is already negative: ~~I can't find it nowhere~~ → I can't find it **anywhere**.

## Frequency: from always to never
The scale: **always → usually → often → sometimes → occasionally → rarely / seldom → hardly ever → never**. For exact frequency we use phrases at the end: **twice a week, every other day, once in a while, from time to time**.
> I **hardly ever** work on Sundays. = I work on Sundays **very rarely**.
> We meet **twice a month**.
> **ever** after a negative adds emphasis: *I don't ever want to see him.* (= I never want to see him.)
- ~~hardly never~~ → **hardly ever** (double negative).

## Time: ago, before, since, for
- **ago** counts back from **now**: *She left three days ago.* (+ past simple)
- **before** counts back from a past moment (past perfect): *She had left three days before.*
- **for** + period, **since** + starting point: *for ten years / since 2015.*
- **already** — earlier than expected; **still** — continuing longer than expected; **yet** — in negatives and questions, 'until now'; **no longer / not ... any more** — no longer true.
> Have you finished **yet**? — I've **already** done it.
> She **still** hasn't replied, and he's **no longer** waiting.

## Time: 'recently' and 'at last'
- **lately / recently**: *I haven't seen her **lately**.* (with perfect) / *He **recently** moved to Rome.* (with simple).
- **just** — 'a moment ago': *The train has **just** left.*
- **finally / at last / eventually / in the end**: **finally** — after waiting; **at last** — with relief; **eventually** — after a long time, often after difficulties; **in the end** — the final result of a process or choice.
> It took hours, but they **eventually** found the road.
- **at the moment / currently** — 'now'; **presently** — 'soon' in BrE, 'now' in AmE.
- **later / afterwards / then / after that**: *Ten years **later** she opened a shop.*

## Common mistakes
- ~~We went to abroad.~~ → We went **abroad**.
- ~~I have seen him yesterday.~~ → I **saw** him yesterday.
- ~~I know him since two years.~~ → I have known him **for** two years.
- ~~She is ill since Monday.~~ → She **has been** ill **since** Monday.
structure:
## Таблица: наречие → значение → пример
| Группа | Наречие | Значение | Пример |
|---|---|---|---|
| Место | **abroad** | за границей / за границу | They work **abroad**. |
| Место | **upstairs / downstairs** | наверху / внизу, наверх / вниз | Come **downstairs**. |
| Направление | **forward(s)** | вперёд | Move **forward**. |
| Частота | **hardly ever** | почти никогда | She **hardly ever** calls. |
| Частота | **twice a week** | дважды в неделю | I swim **twice a week**. |
| Время | **ago** | назад (от сейчас) | It ended **an hour ago**. |
| Время | **lately** | в последнее время | I've felt tired **lately**. |
| Время | **eventually** | в конце концов | They **eventually** agreed. |

## Формулы
> **go / come / move** + наречие места (без предлога): go **home**, move **abroad**
> **have + never/already/just/still** + причастие: has **just** left, hasn't **yet** replied
> past simple + период + **ago**; past perfect + период + **before**
> **for** + длительность; **since** + начало

exercises.title: Подберите наречие
exercises.instruction: Вставьте одно наречие по смыслу (подсказка по-русски).

items.text: She works {{abroad}} for a Swiss company.
The children are playing {{outside|outdoors}} while it's dry.
The bedrooms are {{upstairs}}, and the kitchen is downstairs.
He doesn't work here {{any more|anymore}}; he retired in March.
She is {{still}} waiting for an answer from the committee.
I haven't seen him {{lately|recently}}; is he well?

exercises.title: ago, before, since, for, yet, already

items.text: She told me she had visited Rome two years {{before}}.
We have lived here {{for}} six years.
It's {{already}} midnight, and we haven't had dinner.
He hasn't replied {{yet}}, so I'll call him.
She has {{just}} left, so you may catch her.

items.q: I ___ work on Sundays; it's my day off.
items.why: **hardly ever** — почти никогда; hardly never — двойное отрицание.

items.q: He ___ been late. He's always on time.
items.why: Наречие частоты после has: **has never been**.

items.q: I'm afraid the manager isn't here ___.
The company opened its first shop in 2005; ten years ___, it had 80 branches.
items.why: В рассказе о прошлом — **later**, а не ago.

items.q: She ___ lives in London; she moved to Leeds in May.
The train was delayed twice, but we ___ arrived in Madrid.
A: Is Tom here? B: No, he has ___ left.
The children ran ___ to open the door.
Come ___, and I'll show you the photos.
We looked everywhere, and ___ the key turned up in my coat.
I'm ___ working on a new project, so I can't help.

exercises.title: Перефразируйте
exercises.instruction: Перепишите предложение, используя наречие из скобок.

items.prompt: He doesn't work in this office now. (no longer)
answers: He no longer works in this office.

items.prompt: She goes to the dentist two times each year. (twice a year)
answers: She goes to the dentist twice a year.

items.prompt: I haven't seen her for a few weeks. (lately)
answers: I haven't seen her lately.
I have not seen her lately.

items.prompt: They bought the house ten years before now. (ago)
answers: They bought the house ten years ago.

items.prompt: I'll tell you about it after this. (later)
answers: I'll tell you about it later.
I will tell you about it later.
They have already left the hotel.
They have left the hotel already.
She lives abroad.
She's living abroad.
She is living abroad.
We walked home.
We went home on foot.
We walked back home.
He doesn't work here any more.
He doesn't work here anymore.
He no longer works here.
He does not work here any more.
He does not work here anymore.

items.prompt: Я проверяю почту дважды в день.
answers: I check my email twice a day.
I check my mail twice a day.
I check my e-mail twice a day.
I check my emails twice a day.

items.prompt: Мы в конце концов нашли ключ.
answers: We finally found the key.
We eventually found the key.
In the end, we found the key.
In the end we found the key.
At last we found the key.
At last, we found the key.
Finally, we found the key.
Eventually, we found the key.
Finally we found the key.
Eventually we found the key.
We found the key in the end.
We found the key eventually.
We found the key at last.

exercises.title: Напишите о себе
exercises.instruction: Ответьте полными предложениями, используя наречия места, частоты и времени.

items.prompt: How often do you travel abroad, and where would you like to go?
items.sample: I travel abroad about once a year, and I'd like to go to Japan.

items.prompt: What do you hardly ever do, and what do you do twice a week?
items.sample: I hardly ever watch TV, but I go jogging twice a week.

items.prompt: Describe something that has happened to you lately.
items.sample: Lately I've been working late, so I've hardly had time to cook.

items.prompt: What are you currently doing that you didn't do a year ago?
items.sample: I'm currently learning to play the piano, which I didn't do a year ago.
